findings.title: Viewport meta lacks viewport-fit=cover, so every env(safe-area-inset-*) resolves to 0
findings.description: The viewport meta is `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" />` with no `viewport-fit=cover`. Per the CSS Round Display / WebKit spec, the `env(safe-area-inset-*)` variables only receive non-zero values when the viewport is set to `viewport-fit=cover`; otherwise the layout viewport is inset inside the safe area and all four insets compute to 0px. The codebase relies on these insets in at least 8 places: hotbar height (topbar.css:4-9), topbar padding-top (topbar.css / responsive.css:10,144), note-pane bottom padding (responsive.css:95,148), the mobile bottom action menu (responsive.css:53), and the full-screen search panel (responsive.css:86-87). All of that safe-area code is effectively dead.
findings.why: On an iPhone with a notch/Dynamic Island the topbar and hotbar sit flush against the top edge with no extra inset (the intended `hotbar` accent + inset gradient is only 3px tall), and in the installed PWA the note body's bottom content and the mobile bottom action menu render underneath the home-indicator bar because `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` is 0. The entire notch/home-indicator hardening in this file never activates on the exact clients it targets.
findings.fixSketch: Add `viewport-fit=cover` to the meta: `content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, viewport-fit=cover"`. Then re-test the top/bottom insets on a notched device (see the related double-inset finding before shipping).

findings.title: Hotbar element and topbar padding both add safe-area-inset-top (double top inset once viewport-fit is fixed)
findings.description: `.hotbar` (rendered directly above `.app-topbar` in AppTopbar.tsx:87-88) sets `height: calc(3px + env(safe-area-inset-top))`, consuming the full top inset as a physical element. The topbar that immediately follows ALSO pads by the same inset: `.app-topbar` standalone rule `padding-top: calc(0.9rem + env(safe-area-inset-top))` (responsive.css:144) and the <=920px rule `padding: calc(0.6rem + env(safe-area-inset-top)) ...` (responsive.css:10). The inset is therefore counted twice in the vertical stack.
findings.why: This is latent today because insets are 0 (see the viewport-fit finding), but the moment `viewport-fit=cover` is added the fix will over-correct: on a notched iPhone (~47-59px top inset) the header gains roughly a full extra inset of dead space, pushing the wordmark/actions far down the screen. A fix to one bug silently activates this one.
findings.fixSketch: Pick one consumer of `env(safe-area-inset-top)`. Either keep the hotbar as the inset spacer and drop `env(safe-area-inset-top)` from the topbar padding, or make the hotbar a fixed 3px and let only the topbar pad for the inset.

findings.title: Create/rename modal is vertically centered with 100vh cap and no visualViewport handling, so the on-screen keyboard hides its inputs
findings.description: The write-mode dialog (NoteActionsDialog.tsx:88-102, create/rename/move forms with `<input>`/`<textarea>`) is rendered in `.modal-backdrop` which is `position: fixed; inset: 0; display: flex; align-items: center` (App.css:320-329), and `.modal-panel` is capped at `max-height: min(720px, calc(100vh - 2rem))` (App.css:333). On iOS Safari/WebKit, `100vh` and a `position: fixed; inset:0` layer are sized to the large (keyboard-independent) layout viewport and are NOT shrunk when the software keyboard opens; unlike the mobile drawer top calc (App.tsx:291-306) this modal has no `visualViewport` listener to reposition it.
findings.why: When a user taps a text field to name a new note on iPhone, the keyboard covers the lower ~40-50% of the screen, but the vertically-centered modal stays centered against the full viewport, so the focused input and the create/cancel buttons in `.modal-actions` are pushed behind the keyboard with no way to scroll them into view (the backdrop itself does not scroll). Note creation is effectively blocked on iOS in portrait for anything but the top field.
findings.fixSketch: Use `100dvh` instead of `100vh` for the cap, and/or switch the backdrop to `align-items: flex-start` with a top padding, and add a `visualViewport` resize listener (like App.tsx already does for the drawer) to constrain the modal to `window.visualViewport.height`.

findings.title: Note body and editor textarea have no dir=auto, so RTL vault content renders left-aligned with misplaced punctuation
findings.description: `<html lang="en">` (index.html:2) with no `dir` attribute anywhere, and no `dir="auto"`/`direction` on the rendered note body (`.note-content`/`.note-body`, note-content.css:24-50) or the write-mode editor (`.note-editor-textarea`, note-content.css:80-92; `.modal-panel textarea`, App.css:365). All directional styling is physical: the active-note accent `box-shadow: inset 3px 0 0` (layout-explorer.css:92), tree `border-left` (layout-explorer.css:178), and `padding-left` indents.
findings.why: The vault can legitimately contain Arabic/Hebrew notes. Without `dir="auto"` on the prose container and textarea, RTL paragraphs are rendered as LTR: text hugs the left edge, and trailing punctuation/parentheses jump to the wrong end of the line, making RTL notes hard to read and edit. This is engine-agnostic (all listed clients) but only affects RTL content.
findings.fixSketch: Add `dir="auto"` to the rendered note content wrapper and to both editor textareas so the browser's bidi algorithm picks direction per block from the first strong character.
